Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Nimbus is validating network/evidence for our vendor assessment (CAIQ + SIG). We have a few specific asks around your Private/On‑Prem/Edge deployment patterns so we can map controls to our data flow model: 

1) Canonical placement options: evidence that shows where the control plane, control-plane egress, and data plane terminate for (a) VPC-hosted private, (b) customer-managed on‑prem, and (c) air‑gapped/edge appliances. Diagrams OK.
2) Isolation guarantees between customer workloads when Dedicated hosts multiple customers in the same region (networking + hypervisor/container boundaries).
3) Typical default egress policy for private deployment (ports, outbound domains, cert/key handling).
4) Any automated runbook for emergency isolation (how we can cut control-plane access for an instance).

Can you share artifacts or a short narrative we can use in our SIG/CAIQ answers? We only need what you can share without redacting operational secrets.

Appreciate it — target is our security committee call on Wed 22 Jul.

— Tara

Adding a quick note on the multi‑tenant Dedicated case: our current pattern is to prefer tenant isolation at the VM/container boundary plus strict network ACLs. For Dedicated pools that host multiple tenants (rare, for cost optimization), the enforced controls are:

- Dedicated host affinity (customer tenant pinned to GPU host set)
- Per‑tenant VPC peering + per‑tenant routing tables (no shared NAT)
- Host-level microsegmentation: iptables/ebtables profiles generated from policy service
- Runtime namespacing (container/kata/qemu boundaries) depending on deployment type
- KV cache and model artifacts stored on per‑tenant encrypted volumes (KMS keys scoped to tenant)

I'll attach a short host‑isolation slide and a kernel‑isolation reference (minimal details).

-M

Subject: Private Edge — placement controls package (attachments)

Tara / Nimbus team — attached is a compact package for your committee. Highlights below and a short checklist you can lift into your CAIQ answers: 

Attachments included:
- isolation-diagram-v2.png (diagram: control plane vs data plane boundaries for VPC/private/on‑prem/airgap)
- placement-control-matrix.xlsx (matrix mapping deployment type -> control plane location -> egress behavior -> SIG/CAIQ ref)
- egress-policy-snippets.txt (example iptables + egress FQDN allowlist snippets)
- runbook-private-deploy.pdf (playbook for emergency isolation and control‑plane cutover)

Summary (short):
- Control plane: for Redwood Private we offer a customer‑managed control plane endpoint that is either (a) a dedicated control-plane in the customer VPC (via private link), (b) an on‑prem control plane appliance that talks to management agents over mutual TLS, or (c) an air‑gapped variant that requires scheduled offline syncs. We never mix customer control planes on a shared tenant control plane in Private mode.
- Data plane: model inference runs in customer VPC or on‑prem appliance; network ACLs default to deny inbound, allow minimal outbound to specific control endpoints (mutual TLS, ports 443 + 9411 for tracing) when configured. For air‑gapped installs, outbound is disabled by default; sync is via signed bundle transfer.
- Tenant fencing (Dedicated): per‑tenant host affinity + per‑tenant encrypted volumes + runtime namespacing + per‑tenant routing. Key material is scopped in KMS with CMK per customer.
- Egress: Default deny, explicit allowlist. We publish allowed FQDNs for control-plane endpoints and use short‑lived certs for control agents. Sample snippets attached.
- Emergency isolation: Runbook contains steps to withdraw control‑plane certs, update perimeter ACLs, and place host into maintenance mode; documented rollback.

Next steps / ask:
- Can you confirm if Nimbus needs a redacted BGP / ASN diagram for VPC peering details?
- If you want a CAIQ-ready text block, Laura can draft one that references the exact CAIQ control IDs (NET-1, NET-3, SCH-1, etc.).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20‑minute call if your committee wants a live walkthrough tomorrow.

Best,
Soojin
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
